title: Memory sandbox for KV + activation fractionation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Serving spikes and multi-tenant KV pressure can cause transient OOMs or throttling, forcing conservative static reservations that waste GPU capacity. This ticket proposes a memory 'sandbox' layer that fractionates GPU memory into three logical corridors (weights, KV, activations) with a soft-fence headroom window that can be dynamically loaned and reclaimed during short bursts.

Goal: Improve GPU utilization while preserving safety for production inference by: 1) allowing predictable, bounded transient oversubscribe for KV/activations, 2) providing a simulation and rollout plan to validate safety under mixed continuous-batching workloads, and 3) exposing observability and controls in the Console for tenants and platform operators.
motivation: We currently pad KV/activation reservations to avoid OOMs during token bursts, which reduces throughput and increases cost. A sandbox + fractionation approach should reduce wasted reserved memory by ~8-15% on mixed workloads while keeping P99 latency and SLOs unchanged.
outcome_criteria: 1) No increase in production OOM incidents during canary trials. 2) Measured GPU-reserved wastage reduced by >=8% on target workloads. 3) New telemetry surfaces headroom borrow/reclaim events and a per-tenant safety score. 4) Rollout knobs exist (enable/disable per-cluster, per-tenant, headroom threshold).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by runtime and infra leads
Simulator + stress harness reproduces burst scenarios and verifies reclaim latency < 50ms for typical continuous-batch bursts
Canary on 1 dev cluster with synthetic mixed-priority traffic without increased OOMs for 72h
Console shows headroom utilization, reclaimed bytes, and an alert if reclaim rate > configured threshold
Playbook for manual rollback and emergency static-reserve override created and reviewed
technical_notes:
Core idea: partition the GPU memory budget into soft lanes. We maintain a small immutable weight reservation (W_base) and two soft corridors: KV_soft and ACT_soft. Each corridor has a committed baseline and a transient loan buffer. When a burst occurs KV or activations may borrow from the other's loan buffer up to a configured delta, tracked by a lightweight ledger. Reclaim is policy-driven: immediate reclaim for low-priority loans, gentle reclaim (throttle batching inflight) for high-priority.

Key components: sandbox allocator in runtime, per-request priority tags, ledger + telemetry emitter, prefetch/eviction hooks for KV shards (LRU fallback -> compaction), and admission controller integrated with continuous-batching scheduler. We'll add a simulation module that feeds the real allocator with recorded production traces to validate safety.
implementation_plan: Design spec (this ticket) + API sketch for sandbox control endpoints
Local simulator integration: adapt existing memory-simulator to support soft-loans and mixed-priority replay
Runtime allocator: implement soft-fence bookkeeping and fast-path reclaim path
KV compaction/partial-dehydrate: implement opportunistic compaction when loans exceed threshold
Scheduler integration: admission controller to slow or drop low-priority batches during reclaim
Telemetry: add headroom events, per-tenant reclaimed bytes, loan durations to Console
Canary rollout plan, metrics dashboard, and playbook
tradeoffs: Conservative approach (smaller loan windows) minimizes risk but yields less utilization improvement. Aggressive loans risk mid-batch aborts and possibly higher tail latency. Implementation complexity increases: allocator invariants must be rock-solid. We prioritize safety for initial rollout and increase loan budget incrementally after stable canary results.
risks: 1) Incorrect reclaim timing could cause batch failure mid-token generation. 2) KV compaction latency may spike under pressure. 3) Telemetry lag could delay operator reaction. Mitigations: unit/integration tests for reclaim path, compaction pacing with backoff, and a strict canary with synthetic stress tests.
notes: Prefer a staged rollout: dev cluster -> low-traffic prod -> full prod. Keep emergency static-reserve toggle in Console. Consider tying per-tenant loan budget to the tenant's SLA tier.
